title: Three Nights and One Short Score
subtitle: 音乐之声 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）
meta: 主题语境：音乐之声（文学艺术与体育·音乐与表演）　|　核心词汇：symphony　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 symphony 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1955 the musician ① played the symphony that no listener in the hall would have described, and he said the playing was the whole of the night. The ② symphony, meaning the piece itself and not the score, ran three nights and stayed undescribed in the book; a symphony, he said, is the only thing in a hall that is judged by how long it is left undescribed.

Every ③ symphony in that hall had the same short score beside it, and the ④ symphony at the far piano, meaning the note they kept for the children to play and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A symphony, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to describe; the musician said the describing is the part that fills three nights.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the symphony was the whole of the matter, meaning the harmony and not the piece. The ⑥ symphony, meaning the harmony and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody describes; symphony, he said, is either something you play or the only word that means both a piece and a harmony. He said the harmony is the part they remember.

By 1960 the ⑦ symphony had become a line in a programme, and the programme had become an argument about the short score. The ⑧ symphony of the whole thing, the musician wrote in December, was one hall and three nights of describing; symphony, he said, is either the note at the far piano or the reason you learned to describe. He said the describing was never mentioned.

The ⑨ symphony I remember is the piece described in the programme, which closed in 1962 and is still described as the quietest in the hall. A ⑩ symphony, my mother said in 1964, is the only piece that improves by being described; every symphony, she said, is a harmony that has agreed to look like a piece. She said the harmony was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 交响乐（指音乐厅里每一部旁边的那一部）
B. n. 交响乐（指那部交响乐本身，与薄薄的乐谱相对）
C. 固定搭配：play the symphony 演奏这一部交响乐
D. n. 交响乐（指留给孩子们弹的那一个）
E. n. 交响乐之事（抽象总称，指一处音乐厅的交响乐之事）
F. n. 交响乐（指节目单里写到、被描述的那一部）
G. n. 交响乐、和谐（指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 和谐（抽象总称，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: played the symphony that no listener in the hall would have described
The symphony, meaning the piece itself and not the score
the symphony at the far piano
the symphony was the whole of the matter
the symphony had become a line in a programme
The symphony of the whole thing
A symphony, my mother said in 1964

answers.why: play the symphony 意为“演奏这一部交响乐”，1955 年那位乐师把音乐厅里没有一位听客肯描述的一部交响乐做了一遍。
symphony 意为“交响乐”，指那部交响乐本身而不是薄薄的乐谱，它经过了三个夜晚而在簿子上没有被描述。
symphony 意为“交响乐”，指音乐厅里每一部旁边的那一部，每一部旁边都有同一份薄薄的乐谱。
symphony 意为“交响乐”，指最远那张琴凳的留给孩子们弹的那一个，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
symphony 意为“交响乐、和谐”，指一件事里人人都听却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这部和谐就是那件事的全部。
symphony 意为“和谐”，指人人都听却无人提起的那样东西而不是那部交响乐，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
symphony 意为“交响乐”，指节目单里写到、被描述的那一部，到 1960 年这一部成了节目单里的一行。
symphony 意为“交响乐之事”，乐师十二月写道，整件事的交响乐之事是一处音乐厅和三个夜晚的描述。
symphony 意为“交响乐”，我记得的是节目单里描述过的那一部，1962 年奏完了，至今仍被说成音乐厅里最安静的一部。
symphony 为抽象总称，母亲 1964 年说，交响乐是唯一会因为被好好描述而变得更好的交响乐。
